props.title: The Burning
props.initialSlug: Summer camp slasher stalks teens with garden shears

sections.content: **The Burning** (1981) stands as a pivotal early-80s slasher that helped establish core genre tropes while offering unique twists. Released during the golden age of summer camp horror alongside **Friday the 13th** (1980), it features memorable practical effects from Tom Savini, who had just revolutionized gore effects in **Dawn of the Dead** (1978). The film's killer Cropsey became a legitimate urban legend, influencing later campfire-tale slashers like **Urban Legend** (1998) and **Candyman** (1992).

sections.content: The film's strongest asset is its ensemble cast dynamics, featuring early performances from Jason Alexander and Holly Hunter. Unlike many slashers focused solely on their final girl, **The Burning** develops its teenage characters through genuine interactions and camp politics. This character-driven approach influenced later gems like **The Final Girls** (2015) and **Fear Street: 1978** (2021).

Tom Savini's legendary "raft scene" represents a watershed moment in practical effects. The sequence's shocking brutality and technical excellence stands alongside other genre-defining moments like the chest-burster in **Alien** (1979) and the transformation scenes in **An American Werewolf in London** (1981). Savini's work here directly influenced the graphic practical effects in films like **The Thing** (1982) and **Day of the Dead** (1985). SUBHEAD: Impact on Modern Horror

sections.content: Modern filmmakers continue drawing inspiration from **The Burning**'s blend of urban legend and revenge narrative. **Behind the Mask: The Rise of Leslie Vernon** (2006) directly references Cropsey, while films like **Hatchet** (2006) and **Wrong Turn** (2003) echo its backwoods stalker premise. The film's influence extends to meta-horror like **The Cabin in the Woods** (2012), which deconstructs the tropes **The Burning** helped establish.
